correctness.rationale: For all integers n>=4 and all complex arrays, exact torus character collision counting yields the stated convolution identity. Separate disjoint-matching and adjacent-pair AM-GM majorants combine with alpha=(n-4)/(n-1) into a quadratic form on the complete-graph edge space. The incidence identity BB^T=(n-2)I+J diagonalizes it: both nonconstant eigenvalues are strictly negative, proving C_n and gamma_n for arbitrary dimension. Flat vertex-phase arrays attain the bound and all equality phases factor via matching products. The actual standalone checker.py was run with 1321 exact integer/gaussian-integer assertions in dimensions 4 through 9. Such finite tests supplement, not replace, the analytic n-uniform argument.

originality.rationale: Full primary work on arbitrary-dimensional even-exponent majorants and superorthogonality, and a full published sharp Walsh sign-chaos comparison were read. They do not entail optimization of every complex Steinhaus square-free quadratic edge coefficient, the exact varying C_n, equality gauge, and global magnitude remainder. A known n=4 torus result is strictly subsumed but does not imply n>=5. published-finding corpus semantic searches for Steinhaus, tetrahedral polynomials, Johnson line-graph fourth moments and torus edge packets found no claim covering this theorem. This is best-knowledge priority, not independent certification.

value.rationale: The complete square-free degree-two layer is a natural representation-invariant homogeneous Fourier chaos and exact L2-to-L4 norm problem. The result determines the sharp constant across every n>=4 (first new cases n>=5), complete extremizers, limiting value six, and a globally quantitative coefficient-magnitude rigidity remainder. The proof identifies two different four-cycle majorants and chooses their dimension-sensitive combination to make all nonconstant line-graph eigenspaces negative. This is not an arbitrary parameter slice or a known-table reproduction.
